study type: Retrospective case-control study using machine learning
exposure: low Apgar scores at 1 min and 5 min
cohort: The study included 160 premature neonates admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit, comprising 70 patients with IVH (cases) and 90 without IVH (controls).
finding: A random forest machine learning model effectively predicted Intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) in premature neonates with high accuracy (AUC of 0.99), identifying gestational age, birth weight, low Apgar scores, delivery method, and head circumference as significant risk factors.
mod_finding: Delivery method was identified as a significant risk factor for Intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH).
birth_weight: Applies to premature neonates; specific weight ranges for the cohort are not provided, though birth weight was identified as a risk factor.
gest_age: Applies to premature neonates; specific gestational age ranges for the cohort are not provided, though gestational age was identified as a risk factor.
